rationale: All seven of my round-2 asks are addressed at 4c46cf64, and the three new mechanisms hold up under attack: the lineage selection cannot claim another spec's bead (the `<E>.<N>` prefix and R1.8 (a)/(b) fail closed in every collision I could build), the fallback no longer confirms on a panel alone, and the fingerprint over the complete sorted failure set closes the A-then-A+B hole. Two new completeness gaps remain, both narrow and both in the spec's own stated scope. (1) Lineage selection admits every bd-ready `<E>.<N>` child, including follow-ups filed with `bd create --parent <epic>` that have no `## Bead N` section (this repo has filed such children, e.g. `mindspec-jfgj.4`, a bug under its epic); such a row is selected in bd priority order and then refused by MF-1, so an autopilot loop halts on a bead that today's title filter kept out of the set. The lead's question 'can it select a non-claimable bead?' is answered yes for that class. (2) The spec names its successor `129b`, but `approve/spec.go`'s `parseSpecID` does `strconv.Atoi("129b")`, which fails, so that epic gets `spec_num: 0`; `FindEpicForBead`'s edge leg skips an epic with num 0 and its title fallback parses `[129b-…]` as 129, resolving 129b's own plan beads to spec 129's epic. Under R1.1/R1.8 those beads are N2 for `next --spec 129b` and prefix-mismatched for 129, so the successor spec's beads would be unclaimable via `next`, and readiness/complete would point them at spec 129. Everything else is MINOR.
concrete_changes_required: R1.1: add a plan-section bound to membership, or a near-miss class for its absence. A bd-ready `<E>.<N>` row with lineage E whose N exceeds the plan's declared bead count (the `## Bead N` sections / `work_chunks` that `readiness.EvaluateReadiness` already reads from plan.md) is selected today under R1.1, then refused by MF-1 with no `## Bead N` section — a follow-up filed with `bd create --parent <epic>` (the repo has such children, e.g. `mindspec-jfgj.4`, type bug) can sort first by priority and halt `ms-spec-autopilot` on every scoped `next`. Either (a) membership requires `1 ≤ N ≤ plan bead count` and an overflow row is a new informational near-miss (N4: `bead <id> has the plan-bead form but plan.md declares only <K> beads; readiness would fail MF-1`, recovery `bd show <id> --json`), or (b) state the regression explicitly (today the title filter excludes such rows when their title lacks the full spec ID) and accept it in OQ-9. Add an AC-1 bead `O: <E>.<K+1>, parent E, type bug` with the chosen outcome.

Spec numbering / lettered IDs: `internal/approve/spec.go` `parseSpecID` runs `strconv.Atoi(numStr)` on the text before the first hyphen, so a spec approved as `129b-…` (valid under `idvalidate.specIDPattern`, which allows one trailing letter) gets `spec_num: 0`. `phase.FindEpicForBeadWithCache` skips a parent epic unless `num > 0 && title != ""`, then its title fallback `fmt.Sscanf("129b-…", "%d")` yields 129 and matches spec 129's epic. Consequence under R1.1/R1.8: 129b's own plan beads resolve by lineage to E_129, so `next --spec 129b` classes them N2 and `next --spec 129` rejects them on the `<E>.<N>` prefix — unclaimable — while `ready-check`/`complete` evaluate them against spec 129. Fix: either name the successors with the next plain numbers (and say so in Provenance/OQ-1/Non-Goals), or put the lettered-ID lineage defect in scope / first in the successor, with a Background note and an AC (`TestLineage_LetteredSpecIDResolvesOwnEpic` or an explicit documented limit). Please re-verify `ExtractSpecMetadata`'s title-based fallback for the epic row before choosing.

R1.2 N2: split it. (N2a) row `parent` is another bead P → `bd show <id> --json` (unchanged, never reparent over a named parent). (N2b) NO `parent`, and `FindEpicForBead` resolved another epic through the TITLE fallback → `recovery: bd update <id> --parent <E>` is safe (no parent is overwritten) and is the one edit that also corrects readiness and `complete`, because the parent edge wins over the title in `FindEpicForBeadWithCache`. Name the title-number collision in the message (`lineage resolves to <E2> by title number <NNN>`). Add it to AC-2.

R1.8 (a): state the behaviour change for non-lifecycle beads. `advancePhaseOnClaim` (cmd/mindspec/next.go) documents a non-lifecycle claim (e.g. a `bug` bead with no epic) as a supported `next` outcome today, cut from HEAD; under R1.8 (a) every such claim refuses with 'not a plan bead'. Say this is deliberate, name the alternative for a bug bead (`bd update <id> --claim` plus a manual branch, or filing it under the epic as `<E>.<N>`), add it to the R6.5/R1 doc-surface list where `mindspec next` on bug beads is described, and pin it with an AC-6 leg.

R1.8 (c): before any mutation, verify that `spec/<T>` resolves (`gitutil.RevParseRef`), and refuse naming T when it does not (a finalized spec whose branch was deleted, a spec worktree never created). Otherwise `ClaimBead` succeeds and `DispatchBead` fails on `CreateBranch(…, spec/<T>)`, leaving the claimed-but-homeless state ADR-0041's gate-before-mutate exists to prevent. Add an AC-6 leg.

R6.1/R6.2 consistency on `indeterminate`: R6.2 says an MF-3 `indeterminate` record is never coverable, but R6.1 lets `--allow-not-ready=MF-3 --evidence` claim while MF-3's failure set contains one. The result is a claimed bead whose `ready-check` is permanently non-zero (recovery: release and re-claim, which repeats). Require `GateReadiness` to refuse before mutation when any NAMED failing signal carries an `indeterminate` record (`MF-3 cannot be overridden: <dep> could not be evaluated; fix the read first`), and add an AC-15 leg.

R6.4 coverage rule: fingerprint EQUALITY means a failure set that shrinks (A+B → A after B lands) is uncovered and forces a fresh override, although every remaining failure was vouched. Either state that churn explicitly in R6.4, or store per-record digests (`fingerprints: {<id>: [sha256(record)…]}`) so coverage is 'every current record was recorded' (growth uncovers, shrinkage stays covered); update the validity contract and AC-16 accordingly.

findings.title: Round-2 ask status
findings.detail: F3r2.1 (unscoped claim cut from HEAD) — ADDRESSED: R1.8 (c) makes the lineage spec T the dispatch spec; AC-6 (c) pins the argv seam and the branch base. F3r2.2 (`Merge bead/<id>` is undirected) — ADDRESSED: R4.2 states the form as undirected, admits the two `into <spec-branch>` forms only with this spec as target, requires (b)/(d) on the fallback path, states the residual, and pins it with AC-11 (vii)–(ix); the ADR-0041 amendment item (i) carries the same wording. F3r2.3 (global near-misses drive the exit code) — ADDRESSED: blocking (N1, N2, lifecycle N3 under E) vs informational (title/metadata/non-lifecycle), AC-4 (v)/(vi), OQ-7. F3r2.4 (unlinked ready positional) — ADDRESSED: R1.3 bullet plus AC-3's `TestNext_UnlinkedReadyPositional_Refuses`. F3r2.5 (in-progress re-record has no verb) — ADDRESSED: R6.4's two-line `release` / `next … --evidence` recovery, branch reuse pinned in AC-17; I confirmed `cmd/mindspec/release.go` removes the worktree and sets open without deleting the branch. F3r2.6 (rendered vs raw digest) — ADDRESSED: raw pre-render records, one `FailureFingerprint`, writer/reader control-byte test in AC-16. F3r2.7 (null dependency `parent`) — ADDRESSED: Background C and R4.1 (iii) say it is never read as 'no parent'. No ask of mine is PARTIAL or MISSED; two NEW_ISSUEs are below.

findings.title: Lineage selection admits plan-form children that plan.md does not declare (non-claimable members)
findings.detail: R1.1's predicate is ID form `<E>.<N>` plus lineage E. `bd create --parent <epic>` always mints that form, so a follow-up or bug filed under the epic (this repo has done so: `mindspec-jfgj.4`, type bug, `[073-llm-test-coverage] Fix …`) is a member the moment it is bd-ready, whatever N is. `readiness.evaluateMF1` then fails it ('plan.md has no "## Bead N" section'), so `next --spec S` selects it in bd priority order and refuses NOT-READY — an autopilot loop halts until the row is deprioritised, blocked or overridden. Today the same row is excluded by the title filter whenever its title lacks the full spec ID, so this is a behaviour change the spec does not name. In my scratch db the shape is `lab-rr0.5` (type bug, parent E, title 'manual extra bead'): plan-form, parent edge present, selected under R1.1. The plan's bead count is already available to the binary (readiness parses plan.md's `## Bead` sections and `work_chunks`).

findings.title: A lettered successor ID (`129b`) breaks the lineage this spec now builds selection on
findings.detail: `idvalidate.specIDPattern` admits `^[0-9]{3,}[a-z]?-…`, but `internal/approve/spec.go` `parseSpecID` does `strconv.Atoi(specID[:dashIdx])`, which fails for `129b`, so the epic is created with `spec_num: 0`. `phase.FindEpicForBeadWithCache` honours a parent epic only when `num > 0 && title != ""`, so 129b's own plan beads fall through to the title fallback; `fmt.Sscanf("129b-…", "%d")` reads 129 and the first epic with `spec_num 129` wins — spec 129's. Under R1.1 those beads are N2 for `next --spec 129b` ('lineage resolves to <E_129>') and prefix-mismatched for `next --spec 129`; R1.8 (a) refuses them on every path. `ready-check` would evaluate them against 129's plan and `complete` would merge them into `spec/129`. The spec names `129b` as the home of five deliverables and `129c` as a relief valve. Separately, in a scratch db with two epics carrying `spec_num 129`, the title fallback resolved a detached `[129] …` child of the older epic to the NEWER epic (`bd list --type epic` order is newest-first), i.e. the #255 reporter shape becomes N2 the moment a same-number epic exists.

findings.title: N2 conflates 'parent is another bead' with 'no parent, title lineage elsewhere'
findings.detail: For a plan-form row with NO parent whose lineage resolved to E2 only through the title number, `bd update <id> --parent <E>` overwrites nothing and makes the parent edge win in `FindEpicForBeadWithCache` (verified round 1 and again in this round's scratch db: after `bd update --parent`, `bd show` carries the `parent-child` epic edge). R1.2 gives it only `bd show`, so the one mechanical repair for the collision class is withheld.

findings.title: R1.8 (a) silently retires `mindspec next` for non-lifecycle beads
findings.detail: `advancePhaseOnClaim`'s doc comment names a non-lifecycle claim ('e.g. a `bug` bead') as a supported outcome that advances nothing; such a bead has no `<E>.<N>` ID and today dispatches from HEAD. Under R1.8 (a) it refuses with 'not a plan bead' on both paths. The change is defensible, but it is a user-visible removal that the spec should state, with the alternative and the doc surfaces.

findings.title: R1.8 (c) dispatches into `spec/<T>` without checking it exists
findings.detail: `MindspecExecutor.DispatchBead` runs `gitutil.CreateBranch(branchName, baseBranch)` AFTER `ClaimBead` has succeeded. A stray bd-ready child of a finalized spec (branch deleted) or of a spec whose worktree was never created would be claimed and then fail worktree setup (the existing warn-and-continue), leaving the claimed-but-homeless state. One `RevParseRef` before mutation closes it.

findings.title: `indeterminate` records: claim allowed, coverage impossible
findings.detail: R6.2: 'An MF-3 record of class `indeterminate` … is never coverable'. R6.1: the claim proceeds iff failing ⊆ named, with no exception for indeterminate records. The two together produce a claimed bead whose `ready-check` can never exit 0 until the infrastructure failure is fixed, with a recovery (release + re-claim) that reproduces the state. Refusing the claim when a named failing signal is indeterminate is the fail-closed reading of ADR-0041.

findings.title: Fingerprint equality uncovers a shrinking failure set
findings.detail: With `fingerprints[X] = sha256(sorted records)`, landing one of two failing dependencies changes the digest and uncovers MF-3, forcing a fresh override and evidence for a strictly smaller, already-vouched set. Either state the churn or store per-record digests so subset coverage is checkable. Growth (A → A+B) must stay uncovered either way.

findings.title: Attacks that did not land (verified)
findings.detail: Can lineage selection claim another spec's bead? No: membership needs the `<E>.<N>` prefix AND lineage E, and R1.8 (a)/(b) re-check both with the lineage spec; every collision I built (same-number epics, `[128]`-titled child under E with the parent edge present, detached `[128]`-titled `<E>.N`, a 129b bead) ends in N2 or a refusal, never a cross-spec claim. In the scratch db a child with the parent edge and a foreign `[128-other]` title (`lab-rr0.2`) still resolves to E through the edge, so a mis-titled plan bead stays selectable (correct). Fallback confirmation: panel-only match → NoEvidence; (b)/(d) on the fallback are the stated residual; ambiguity resolved only by a corroborated single group with no contradicting datum. R4.3's reach into CLOSE paths is safe as argued ({A,B} with B exact confirms; {A} alone refuses). `bd ready` rows carry `parent`/`metadata` when set (re-measured). BRIEF Round-3 refutation of my round-2 'TODO(skill) placeholders remain' is correct: at HEAD `grep -n 'TODO(skill)'` hits only line 86, the Round-3 text quoting the refuted claim; my round-2 finding was carried from round-1 memory and was wrong. No worktree was created; the scratch bd db under r3/F3 is removed.

findings.title: Errors in this BRIEF
findings.detail: (1) Line 12 of the machine header still instructs `<your-slot>-round-3.json` beside this BRIEF; line 66 corrects it to the scratch path. The header template should carry the correct rule rather than being overridden below. (2) The Round 3 section says 'Selection = every bd-ready `<E>.<N>` bead whose unchanged FindEpicForBead lineage is E, whether or not a parent edge exists' — accurate, but it omits that lineage may come from the `[NNN]` title fallback, which is the property both new MAJOR findings turn on; a reviewer reading only the BRIEF would not know to attack it. (3) Otherwise none found: the round-2 tally (2 APPROVE / 7 RC, 36 asks), the fix commit and the change list match the consolidation and the spec text.
